subject.title: fix(codex): cap compaction override warning cache via createDedupeCache

question: Should ignored OpenClaw compaction overrides for Codex remain process-lifetime warn-once, reset with the configured-agent lifecycle, or re-warn after a generic 4096-key eviction?
rationale: The implementation is correct, but the retention policy changes user-visible diagnostics and cannot be selected safely from synthetic mechanics alone, especially after the adjacent maintainer decision rejected the same unsupported tradeoff.

options.title: Use configured-agent lifecycle
options.body: Reset or bound warning state at the canonical config or agent-registry lifecycle and add focused coverage for that ownership boundary.

options.title: Approve generic eviction
options.body: Accept the 4096-key LRU and possible repeated warnings after eviction as intentional defensive behavior.

options.title: Keep process-lifetime suppression
options.body: Retain the current Set until observed production growth demonstrates a meaningful resource problem.

recommendation.title: Use configured-agent lifecycle
recommendation.body: Reset or bound warning state at the canonical config or agent-registry lifecycle and add focused coverage for that ownership boundary.
